In [[mathematics]], '''von Neumann's theorem''' is a result in the [[operator theory]] of [[linear operator]]s on [[Hilbert space]]s. 

==Statement of the theorem==

Let <math>G</math> and <math>H</math> be Hilbert spaces, and let <math>T : \operatorname{dom}(T) \subseteq G \to H</math> be an [[unbounded operator]] from <math>G</math> into <math>H.</math> Suppose that <math>T</math> is a [[closed operator]] and that <math>T</math> is [[Densely defined operator|densely defined]], that is, <math>\operatorname{dom}(T)</math> is [[Dense (topology)|dense]] in <math>G.</math> Let <math>T^* : \operatorname{dom}\left(T^*\right) \subseteq H \to G</math> denote the [[Adjoint operator|adjoint]] of <math>T.</math> Then <math>T^* T</math> is also densely defined, and it is [[self-adjoint]]. That is,
<math display=block>\left(T^* T\right)^* = T^* T</math>
and the operators on the right- and left-hand sides have the same dense domain in <math>G.</math><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Acuña|first=Pablo|date=2021|title=von Neumann's Theorem Revisited|url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/s10701-021-00474-5|journal=Foundations of Physics|language=en|volume=51|issue=3|pages=73|doi=10.1007/s10701-021-00474-5|bibcode=2021FoPh...51...73A |s2cid=237887405 |issn=0015-9018|url-access=subscription}}</ref>
